summary.intent: Resolve PR review comments on a docs branch, then perform a comprehensive documentation audit and update covering DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md, codebase maps, and a new filesystem specification document.
summary.outcome: PR #419 was created and merged with 15 commits across 10 files. DEFERRED.md was thoroughly audited and pruned of implemented/out-of-scope items. Phases 38 (retire folder.service.ts/bin.service.ts) and 39 (user-configurable vault parameters) were added to the roadmap. A new FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md was created. All docs/ files were updated to reflect phases 28-37 changes.

repo: Grafana Faro is the error tracking and remote log shipping solution — not Sentry. Configured in apps/web/src/lib/faro.ts with beforeSend scrubbing.
RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS is an operator env var, not a user-facing setting — the deferred item for user-configurable bin retention is still valid.

TEE republish uses Phala Cloud CVM (Phase 35). Pre-migration enrollments fail with 'ECIES decryption failed for all available epochs' because they were wrapped with the old TEE public key. 477 new enrollments are correct; 15 stale ones will use DB-cached CID fallback.
FUSE unit tests are intentionally absent — the FUSE layer is pure OS plumbing between macOS/Linux/Windows and the Rust SDK. Coverage comes from Desktop E2E test suite instead.
folder.service.ts (1,059 lines, 9 importers) and bin.service.ts (971 lines, 2 functions actually used) are the primary retirement targets for Phase 38.
@cipherbox/crypto has @cipherbox/core as a devDependency only for a test in vault-ipns.test.ts that compares key derivation. This was meant to be removed during Phase 19.1 restructuring.
Duplicate file upload path (replace/duplicate branch) still uses encryptFile() on main thread — Phase 37 moved new file encryption to Web Worker but missed this code path.
SDK packages (sdk, sdk-core) use console.warn bypassing the Faro transport since they are zero-dependency packages. 11+ console.warn calls exist that don't go through structured logging.
IPNS keys republish on a 6-hour cycle (not 3h as previously documented). The TEE batch runs at scheduled intervals and TEE health endpoint at /health returns epoch info.

The CipherBox filesystem enforces Windows-compatible naming as the strictest common denominator (case-insensitive, 255-char limit, reserved names like CON/PRN/AUX). macOS and Linux FUSE mounts are case-sensitive but the naming rules enforce the Windows-safe subset.
AES-CTR is used for large files (audio and video), not just video. AES-GCM is used for smaller files. The FUSE layer streams CTR decryption; uploads also use CTR for large files client-side.
Linux FUSE uses the same fuse feature flag as macOS — NFC-normalized, case-sensitive. Accessible via terminal. Windows mount accessible via PowerShell and Git Bash.
share_invites and pin_migrations are tables that exist in the DB but were missing from DATABASE_EVOLUTION_PROTOCOL.md. Total is 14 tables, not 12.
Phase 35 removed the Docker TEE simulator entirely, leaving Phala Cloud CVM as the single TEE provider with no fallback option.

code.finding: Grafana Faro implementation — handles error tracking, structured logging, and remote log shipping to Grafana Cloud with beforeSend scrubbing for PII
Added try/catch around getWorker()/postMessage() to prevent pending map leaks on throw
uploadFiles() doc comment was updated to clarify memory bounding — large files use streaming CTR, only small files are fully buffered

Imports @cipherbox/core only to compare deriveRegistryIpnsKeypair vs deriveVaultIpnsKeypair for domain separation test. This devDependency was supposed to be cleaned up in Phase 19.1 — scheduled for Phase 38.
TEE republish failures return HTTP 200 with success:false in result objects — the error detail (ECIES decryption failed) is not logged at service level, only visible in the republish_schedule table
Contains is_platform_special() and is_windows_special() for reserved name enforcement across platforms
Filesystem constants including name length limits and reserved character sets

New document created this session. Covers naming rules, per-platform case handling, reserved names, size/quota/depth limits, versioning constraints, FUSE mount specifics, encryption modes (GCM vs CTR), and cross-platform gaps.

workflow: When asked to audit and prune a list, do each item systematically rather than relying on spot-checks triggered by user corrections. Shallow passes waste multiple rounds of follow-up.
gh api GraphQL reviewThreads returns isResolved status. REST endpoint for replies requires --field in_reply_to=INT (not -f), then GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation to mark resolved.
gsd-codebase-mapper agents write documents directly and return only line counts + confirmation — orchestrator never receives document contents, keeping context minimal.
The Task tool supports run_in_background=true for parallel agent spawning; use TaskOutput with block:true to wait for completion.
gh pr create returns URL directly; gh pr edit --body can update existing PR descriptions.

When a devDependency creates a conceptual circular dependency in a monorepo, check whether it's test-only before flagging as an issue — test devDeps are generally fine but may indicate a test organization smell.

friction: Multiple rounds of user correction needed for DEFERRED.md audit — the first pass removed only 3 items user explicitly mentioned, missing many others that were obviously implemented (Grafana Faro, Linux FUSE, CTR streaming, etc.).
RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS was incorrectly identified as implementing the user-facing retention preference, then had to be reverted — operator config vs user-facing settings are distinct.
The Edit tool reformatted table cell widths in markdown tables, requiring extra verification steps to confirm the actual file content before making subsequent edits.
Committing required multiple retries due to commit message format issues (parentheses in subject line failing hooks, requiring dashes instead).
TEE republish failure root cause was not logged at the TeeService level — had to query the republish_schedule table directly via psql to find the ECIES decryption error.
useDropUpload.ts hook has no unit tests despite being significantly rewritten in Phase 37 as the primary upload entry point — a gap noted in CONCERNS.md but not addressed this session.
open_items: Phase 38: Retire folder.service.ts (1,059 lines, 9 importers) and bin.service.ts (971 lines) by migrating callers to SDK methods. Also includes removing @cipherbox/crypto devDependency on @cipherbox/core by refactoring vault-ipns.test.ts to use hardcoded test vectors.

Phase 39: User-configurable vault parameters — bin retention period (user-chosen days, default 30), delete behavior (soft vs hard delete), versioning defaults (max versions per file, version cooldown period).

15 stale TEE republish entries failing with ECIES decryption error — wrapped for old TEE public key pre-Phase 35. Left as-is; DB-cached CID fallback handles resolution until clients reconnect and re-enroll.

Duplicate file upload path (replace/duplicate branch in useDropUpload.ts) still encrypts on main thread — Phase 37 moved new file encryption to Web Worker but missed this branch. Noted in CONCERNS.md.
SDK packages (sdk, sdk-core) use console.warn bypassing Faro transport — 11+ calls need structured logging migration. Noted in CONCERNS.md.
useDropUpload.ts hook has no unit tests despite Phase 37 making it the primary upload entry point. Noted in CONCERNS.md.
Phala Cloud CVM is single TEE provider with no fallback — Docker simulator was removed in Phase 35. Noted in CONCERNS.md as fragile.
@phala/dstack-sdk single-provider lock-in noted as dependency at risk in CONCERNS.md.
Faro telemetry scrub relies on key-name allow-list — new attack surface from Phase 30, noted in CONCERNS.md as security concern.
